as

\matrixelement{\text{out}+1}{S}{\text{in}}=\sqrt{8\pi}\quantity(\sum_{\substack{i\\\text{out}}} \frac{\tensor*{p}{^i_\mu}\tensor*{p}{^i_\nu}}{\tensor*{p}{_i^\rho}\tensor{q}{_\rho}} - \sum_{\substack{j\\\text{in}}} \frac{\tensor*{p}{^j_\mu}\tensor*{p}{^j_\nu}}{\tensor*{p}{_j^\rho}\tensor{q}{_\rho}})^{\text{TT}}\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}(q)\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S}{\text{in}}+\order{\tensor{q}{^0}}.

(322)

Using these results,
[
241
,
242
]
showed that

\absolutevalue{\mel{\text{out}'}{S}{\text{in}}}^{2}=\absolutevalue{\mel{\text{out}'}{S}{\text{in}}}^{2}b(B)\quantity(\frac{E}{\lambda})^{B},

(323)

for the same positive constant
B
of
Eq.

319
and for some real function
b(x)
. Using both
Eqs.

319
and
323
, we find the final result

\absolutevalue{\mel{\text{out}'}{S}{\text{in}}}^{2}=\absolutevalue{\mel{\text{out}}{S^0}{\text{in}}}^{2}b(B)\quantity(\frac{E}{\Lambda})^{B},

(324)

which is now well-defined and finite in the
\lambda\to 0
limit.

The lesson to be taken is that in any scattering process an infinite number of soft gravitons will be emitted. This is imposed by the
\gls
IR structure of
\gls
GR and required for the scattering probability to be non-vanishing.

The natural question at this point is: what does this have to do with the
\gls
BMS group?

Despite both the Weinberg soft theorem and the
\gls
BMS group being discovered in the 1960’s, the relation between them would only become clear in the 2010’s.
[
224
,
he2015BMSSupertranslationsWeinberg
]
noticed that the Weinberg soft graviton theorem is actually a consequence of
\gls
BMS invariance of gravitational scattering. More specifically, the Weinberg soft graviton theorem is equivalent to the Ward identity (
294
), as we shall show. The upshot is that the Weinberg soft graviton theorem and the supertranslations in the
\gls
BMS group are two related aspects of the
\gls
IR structure of
\gls
GR.

To push this analogy further, one can notice that the charges
Q^{\pm}_{f}
act non-trivially on the Minkowski vacuum. This is expected, since we saw in
Section

6.1
that the
\gls
GR vacuum is not supertranslation-invariant. The action of these supertranslation charges is to create a soft graviton
[
224
,
225
]
, meaning we can understand the soft gravitons as the
\glspl
NGB associated to the spontaneous symmetry breaking of supertranslation symmetry.

This sheds light on the nature of the different vacua in gravity. A choice of vacuum in quantum gravity will determine what is the “absence of soft gravitons”. Other vacua are then interpreted as having various numbers of soft gravitons. The number of soft gravitons is to be understood only in relational terms, as any of these vacua are equally allowed to be taken as “the” vacuum.

Weinberg predicted that in any scattering experiment there will be the emission of soft gravitons. This is, therefore, a vacuum transition, and it is a quantum point of view of the classical vacuum transitions we found in
Section

6.2
.

Let us then prove this connection is real. I follow the discussion of the original paper by
[
he2015BMSSupertranslationsWeinberg
]
. Notice the Weinberg soft graviton theorem was formulated in terms of creation and annihilation operators for the graviton field
\mathchoice{h^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{h^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{h^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{h^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}
, but the Ward identity on
Eq.

304
is written in terms of the Bondi news tensor
\mathchoice{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}
. Therefore, we need to convert from one to the other.

We start by considering the quantization of the gravitational field (see Sec. 2 of Ref.
\citeonline
basile2024LecturesQuantumGravity for an introduction to perturbative quantum gravity). Near null infinity, it can be taken to be approximately free. Therefore, in Cartesian coordinates, we can make an expansion in creation and annihilation operators according to

\mathchoice{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(x)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3}}\sum_{\lambda=+,-}\int\quantity[\tensor*{\epsilon}{^{\lambda}^*_\mu_\nu}(\vb{q}) \hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vb{q}) e^{i q \cdot x} + \tensor*{\epsilon}{^{\lambda}_\mu_\nu}(\vb{q}) \hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vb{q})^\dagger e^{-i q \cdot x}]\frac{\differential[3]{q}}{2\omega_{\vec{\boldsymbol{q}}}}.

(325)

Notice
\lambda
runs over the two polarizations of the graviton. In this convention, the commutation relations for the ladder operators are

\commutator{\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vb{q})}{\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\mu}(\vb{p})^\dagger}=(2\omega_{\vec{\boldsymbol{q}}})(2\pi)^{3}\delta_{\lambda,\mu}\delta^{(3)}\quantity(\vb{q}-\vb{p}).

(326)

This is the same convention we implicitly assumed when deriving the Weinberg soft graviton theorem: an outgoing state with one extra graviton is obtained by acting with
\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})
on the outgoing bra (or with
\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})^{\dagger}
on the outgoing ket). Furthermore,
Eq.

325
implies the polarization of an outgoing graviton is given by
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}
, not
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}
.

We will slowly change coordinates to retarded stereographic coordinates. The first step is to rewrite the null vectors
\mathchoice{q^{{{a}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.59009pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.85005pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{a}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.59009pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.85005pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{a}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.59009pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.85005pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{a}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.33765pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.59009pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.85005pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}
in stereographic coordinates. If
\vec{\boldsymbol{q}}
points to the point in the sphere with stereographic coordinate
\chi
, we get the Cartesian components

\mathchoice{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}=\frac{\omega_{\vec{\boldsymbol{q}}}}{1+\chi\bar{\chi}}\quantity(1 + \chi\bar{\chi},\chi+ \bar{\chi},-i(\chi- \bar{\chi}),-1 + \chi\bar{\chi}).

(327)

This expression comes from
Eq.

137
.

This is useful for us to write the polarization tensors. The polarization tensors must be symmetric, transverse (
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})\mathchoice{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}=0
) and traceless (
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})\mathchoice{\eta^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\eta^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\eta^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\eta^{{{\mu}{\nu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}=0
). This can be achieved by defining
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})=\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})
, where the polarization vectors
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}}}_{{{\mu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})
are the same ones used in electrodynamics and can be taken to be

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\quantity(\bar{\chi},1,- i, \bar{\chi}),

(328a)

and

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{-}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{\mu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{q}})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\quantity(\chi,1,+i, \chi).

(328b)

where
\mathchoice{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{q^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}
and the stereographic coordinate
\chi
are related by
Eq.

327
.

We can now write the shear tensor
\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}
as

\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}=\sqrt{32\pi}\lim_{r\to+\infty}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\tensor{x}{^A}}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\tensor{x}{^B}}\frac{\mathchoice{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\hat{h}^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(u,r,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})}{r}.

(329)

In terms of creation and annihilation operators we find

\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}(u,\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})=\frac{\sqrt{32\pi}}{(2\pi)^{3}}\lim_{r\to+\infty}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\tensor{x}{^A}}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\tensor{x}{^B}}\frac{1}{r}\sum_{\lambda=+,-}\int\quantity[\tensor*{\epsilon}{^{\lambda}^*_\mu_\nu}(\vb{q}) \hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\vb{q}) e^{- i \omega_{\vb{q}} u - i \omega_{\vb{q}} r (1 - \vu{q} \vdot\vu{x})} + \Hc]\frac{\differential[3]{q}}{2\omega_{\vec{\boldsymbol{q}}}},

(330)

with
H.c.
denoting the Hermitian conjugate.

We can compute the angular integral in
Eq.

330
to leading order in
r
by employing the stationary phase approximation—see Appendix
E
and, in particular,
Eq.

649
. We find

\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}(u,\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})=-\frac{i\sqrt{32\pi}}{8\pi^{2}}\lim_{r\to+\infty}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\tensor{x}{^A}}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\tensor{x}{^B}}\frac{1}{r^{2}}\sum_{\lambda=+,-}\int\left[\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\omega\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})e^{-i\omega u}\right.\\
\left.+\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(-\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(-\omega\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})e^{-i\omega u-2i\omega r}-\textrm{H.c.}\right]\differential{\omega},

(331)

I flipped the sign on
H.c.
because we pulled out a factor of
i
from inside the integral. The antipodal modes on the second line will not survive up to
\mathscr{I}^{+}
: the exponential behaves as
e^{-i\omega v}
and oscillates too much. A stationary phase approximation will ensure the term vanishes at future null infinity (see Theorem 7.7.1 in Ref.
\citeonline
hormander2003DistributionTheoryFourier). We thus find

\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}(u,\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})=-\frac{i\sqrt{32\pi}}{8\pi^{2}}\lim_{r\to+\infty}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\tensor{x}{^A}}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\tensor{x}{^B}}\frac{1}{r^{2}}\sum_{\lambda=+,-}\int\left[\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\lambda}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{\lambda}(\omega\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})e^{-i\omega u}-\textrm{H.c.}\right]\differential{\omega},

(332)

Since
\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{A}{B}}}}
is real and traceless, the component
\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}
is sufficient to describe the tensor in stereographic coordinates (
\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}}=0

Using the expressions for the Cartesian coordinates in terms of stereographic coordinates (these were given in

that

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(\chi,\bar{\chi})

\displaystyle=\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\zeta}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\zeta}\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}=\frac{2r^{2}\bar{\zeta}^{2}(\bar{\zeta}-\bar{\chi})^{2}}{(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{4}},

(333a)

and

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(\chi,\bar{\chi})

\displaystyle=\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\zeta}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\zeta}\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}=\frac{2r^{2}(1+\bar{\zeta}\chi)^{2}}{(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{4}}.

(333b)

In spite of these expressions, it is important to notice that the definitions of the polarization tensors imply that
\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\pm}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\pm}{*}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}=\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{\mp}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mp}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mp}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{\mp}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}
, and hence

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(\chi,\bar{\chi})

\displaystyle=\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\zeta}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\zeta}\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}=\frac{2r^{2}(1+\bar{\zeta}\chi)^{2}}{(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{4}},

(333c)

and

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{-}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{\epsilon^{{{-}{*}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(\chi,\bar{\chi})

\displaystyle=\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\mu}}{\zeta}\partialderivative{\tensor{x}{^\nu}}{\zeta}\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}=\frac{2r^{2}\bar{\zeta}^{2}(\bar{\zeta}-\bar{\chi})^{2}}{(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{4}}.

(333d)

At
\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}=\boldsymbol{\hat{x}}
we get
\zeta=\chi
(and
\bar{\zeta}=\bar{\chi}
). Hence,

and

now yield

\mathchoice{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{C^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(u,{\zeta},\bar{\zeta})=\frac{-i\sqrt{32\pi}}{4\pi^{2}(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\int\left[\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{+}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})e^{-i\omega u}-\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{-}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})^{\dagger}e^{+i\omega u}\right]\differential{\omega}.

(334)

We now have the shear tensor. The next step is to get to the Bondi news tensor. A time derivative yields

\mathchoice{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(u,{\zeta},\bar{\zeta})=\frac{-\sqrt{32\pi}}{4\pi^{2}(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\int_{0}^{+\infty}\omega\left[\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{+}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})e^{-i\omega u}+\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{-}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})^{\dagger}e^{+i\omega u}\right]\differential{\omega},

where the “out” superscript indicates this is the Bondi news tensor at
\mathscr{I}^{+}
(as opposed to
\mathscr{I}^{-}
).

Notice that

\int\mathchoice{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{{\text{out}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}(u,{\zeta},\bar{\zeta})\differential{u}=\frac{-\sqrt{32\pi}}{4\pi(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\lim_{\omega\to 0^{+}}\quantity[\omega\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{+}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) + \omega\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{-}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})^{\dagger}],

(336)

where we used that the
\omega=0
Fourier mode is the average of the limits
\omega\to 0^{+}
and
\omega\to 0^{-}
. This is the definition used in Ref.
\citeonline
he2015BMSSupertranslationsWeinberg and it is necessary because the integral on

only runs over half of the real line.

To meet with
Eq.

304
, we now consider the object

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{out}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(u,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{u} S}{\text{in}}=\frac{-\sqrt{32\pi}}{4\pi(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\lim_{\omega\to 0^{+}}\omega\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{+}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) S}{\text{in}}.

(337)

In the previous expressions, we used the fact that
\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{-}(\omega,\zeta)^{\dagger}
annihilates the outgoing state for
\omega\to 0
. If
\ket{\text{out}}
contains soft gravitons, this still holds, because our definition of annihilation operators multiplies the state by a factor of

(see
Eq.

326

\omega\to 0
limit.

Similarly we find that

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S \int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{in}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(v,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{v}}{\text{in}}=\frac{-\sqrt{32\pi}}{4\pi(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\lim_{\omega\to 0^{+}}\omega\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S \hat{a}^{\text{in}}_{-}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta})}{\text{in}}.

(338)

Diagramatically we can see that an incoming graviton with negative helicity with energy
\omega
coming in from the direction
\zeta
(as defined on
\mathscr{I}^{-}
) contributes to the overall amplitude in precisely the same way as an outgoing graviton with positive helicity, energy
\omega
, and puncturing
\mathscr{I}^{+}
at
\zeta
. Therefore, we may write

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{out}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(u,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{u} S + S \int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{in}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(v,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{v}}{\text{in}}\\
=\frac{-\sqrt{32\pi}}{2\pi(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})^{2}}\lim_{\omega\to 0^{+}}\omega\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\hat{a}^{\text{out}}_{+}(\omega,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) S}{\text{in}}.

(339)

The
\gls
LHS of this expression is one covariant derivative away from the
\gls
LHS of
Eq.

304

To simplify the

. We get

\displaystyle\mathchoice{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}

(342a)

\displaystyle\mathchoice{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}

\displaystyle=\frac{E_{i}}{1+\zeta_{i}\bar{\zeta}_{i}}\quantity(1 + \zeta_i \bar{\zeta}_i,\zeta_i + \bar{\zeta}_i,-i(\zeta_i - \bar{\zeta}_i),-1 + \zeta_i \bar{\zeta}_i),

(342b)

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}{\epsilon^{{{+}{\mu}}}}(\zeta,\bar{\zeta})

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\quantity(\bar{\zeta},1,-i,\bar{\zeta}).

(342c)

These expressions all follow from
Eqs.

328
and
327
.
\zeta_{i}
denote the points in the celestial sphere punctured by the particles with momenta
\mathchoice{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}{p^{{{\mu}}}_{{{i}}}}
.
E_{i}
denote the energy carried by each of these particles. Using these expressions we find

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{out}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(u,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{u} S + S \int\tensor*{N}{^{\text{in}}_{\zeta}_\zeta}\qty(v,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{v}}{\text{in}}\\
=\frac{8}{(1+\zeta\bar{\zeta})}\quantity(\sum_{\substack{i\\\text{out}}} \frac{E_i^{\text{out}} (\bar{\zeta} - \bar{\zeta}_i^{\text{out}})}{(\zeta- \zeta_i^{\text{out}})(1 + \zeta_i^{\text{out}} \bar{\zeta}_i^{\text{out}})} - \sum_{\substack{j\\\text{in}}} \frac{E_j^{\text{in}} (\bar{\zeta} - \bar{\zeta}_j^{\text{in}})}{(\zeta- \zeta_j^{\text{in}})(1 + \zeta_j^{\text{in}} \bar{\zeta}_j^{\text{in}})})\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S}{\text{in}}.

(343)

One can check that

\mathchoice{D^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{D^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{D^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{D^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}\mathchoice{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{A}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{A}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{A}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{A}}}}=\mathchoice{{}^{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{{}^{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{{}^{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{{}^{{{\zeta}{\bar{\zeta}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}\mathchoice{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\bar{\zeta}}}}}{\partial^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[5.00002pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\bar{\zeta}}}}}\mathchoice{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}{N^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\zeta}{\zeta}}}}.

(344)

Using this expression, we conclude that

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\int\tensor{D}{^A}\tensor*{N}{^{\text{out}}_{\zeta}_A}\qty(u,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{u} S + S \int\tensor{D}{^A}\tensor*{N}{^{\text{in}}_{\zeta}_A}\qty(v,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{v}}{\text{in}}\\
=4\quantity(\sum_{\substack{i\\\text{out}}} \frac{E_i^{\text{out}}}{\zeta- \zeta_i^{\text{out}}} - \sum_{\substack{j\\\text{in}}} \frac{E_j^{\text{in}}}{\zeta- \zeta_j^{\text{in}}})\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S}{\text{in}}\\
+4\quantity(\sum_{\substack{i\\\text{out}}} \frac{E_i^{\text{out}} \bar{\zeta}_i^{\text{out}}}{1 + \zeta_i^{\text{out}} \bar{\zeta}_i^{\text{out}}} - \sum_{\substack{j\\\text{in}}} \frac{E_j^{\text{in}} \bar{\zeta}_j^{\text{in}}}{1 + \zeta_j^{\text{in}} \bar{\zeta}_j^{\text{in}}})\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S}{\text{in}}.

(345)

Momentum conservation forces the last line to vanish. We thus find that the Weinberg soft graviton theorem can be written as

\matrixelement{\text{out}}{\int\tensor{D}{^A}\tensor*{N}{^{\text{out}}_{\zeta}_A}\qty(u,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{u} S + S \int\tensor{D}{^A}\tensor*{N}{^{\text{in}}_{\zeta}_A}\qty(v,\zeta,\bar{\zeta}) \dd{v}}{\text{in}}\\
=4\quantity(\sum_{\substack{i\\\text{out}}} \frac{E_i^{\text{out}}}{\zeta- \zeta_i^{\text{out}}} - \sum_{\substack{j\\\text{in}}} \frac{E_j^{\text{in}}}{\zeta- \zeta_j^{\text{in}}})\matrixelement{\text{out}}{S}{\text{in}}.

(346)

Reverting the calculations allows us to reobtain the soft theorem from this expression. Furthermore, this expression is identical to
Eq.

304
, which in turn is equivalent to the Ward identity for supertranslations. We conclude that the Weinberg soft graviton theorem is indeed the Ward identity for supertranslations.

6.5
Gravitational Memory Effect

The
\gls
GW displacement memory effect
[
255
,
40
,
41
,
59
,
229
,
32
]
was originally discovered in linearized gravity by
[
255
]
. It consists on the prediction that the passage of a
\gls
GW permanently displaces the relative positions of two nearby inertial detectors stationed near infinity. It turns out that this effect is too a reflection of
\gls
BMS transformations. Let us then derive the memory effect and see how this correspondence occurs. I will work in the framework of linearized gravity, but there are more powerful results in full
\gls
GR. I follow
[
41
,
29
]
.

We consider two nearby inertial detectors, initially at rest relative to each other, stationed “near infinity”. This means that when we perform a large-
r
(or small-
l
) expansion we can neglect the subleading terms. Write the separation between these two detectors as
\mathchoice{d^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{d^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{d^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{d^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}+\mathchoice{\Delta x^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Delta x^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Delta x^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Delta x^{{{i}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}(t)
, where

and we assume

is small compared to

]

Our task is then to compute

\text{in}\end{subarray}}\frac{\mathchoice{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}}{{}_{p}}\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{n!}\left\lfloor\derivative[n]{t}\int\delta^{(3)}\quantity(\vb{y} - t\vb{v}_p)\quantity(\vu{x} \vdot\vb{y})^{n}\differential[3]{y}\right\rfloor+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}},

(354a)

\displaystyle=\frac{4}{r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\\
\text{in}\end{subarray}}\frac{\mathchoice{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}}{{}_{p}}\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{n!}\left\lfloor\derivative[n]{t}t^{n}\quantity(\vu{x} \vdot\vb{v}_p)^{n}\right\rfloor+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}},

(354b)

\displaystyle=\frac{4}{r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\\
\text{in}\end{subarray}}\frac{\mathchoice{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}}{{}_{p}}\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}\quantity(\vu{x} \vdot\vb{v}_p)^{n}+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}},

(354c)

\displaystyle=\frac{4}{r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\\
\text{in}\end{subarray}}\frac{\mathchoice{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}}{{}_{p}\quantity(1 - \vu{x} \vdot\vb{v}_p)}+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}}.

(354d)

Above, as in Appendix
C
,
\lfloor\cdot\rfloor
denotes evaluation at retarded time
u=t-r
, but this turned out to be irrelevant.

Introduce the null vector
\mathchoice{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}=(1,\boldsymbol{\hat{x}})
, which points from the source to the observation point. In terms of this null vector we find that

\mathchoice{\bar{h}^{{{\text{in}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\bar{h}^{{{\text{in}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\bar{h}^{{{\text{in}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}{\bar{h}^{{{\text{in}}}}_{{{\mu}{\nu}}}}(t,\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})=-\frac{4}{r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\\
\text{in}\end{subarray}}\frac{\mathchoice{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}{p^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\mu}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}{u^{{{(p)}}}_{{{\nu}}}}}{\mathchoice{k^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\rho}}}}{k^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\rho}}}}{k^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\rho}}}}{k^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{\rho}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{{(p)}{\rho}}}}{u^{{{(p)}{\rho}}}}{u^{{{(p)}{\rho}}}}{u^{{{(p)}{\rho}}}}}+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}}.

(355)

At last, we find that the change in the gravitational field between early and late times is given, in
\gls
TT gauge, by

\mathchoice{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}(\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})=-\frac{4}{r}\quantity[\sum_{\substack{p \\ \text{out}}} \frac{\tensor*{p}{^{(p)}_i} \tensor*{p}{^{(p)}_j}}{\tensor{k}{_\rho} \tensor*{p}{^{(p)}^\rho}} - \sum_{\substack{q \\ \text{in}}} \frac{\tensor*{p}{^{(q)}_i} \tensor*{p}{^{(q)}_j}}{\tensor{k}{_\rho} \tensor*{p}{^{(q)}^\rho}}]^{\text{TT}}+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}},

(356)

where we used
\mathchoice{p^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{p^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{p^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{p^{{{(q)}{a}}}}=m_{q}\mathchoice{u^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{u^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{u^{{{(q)}{a}}}}{u^{{{(q)}{a}}}}
to get an expression in terms of momenta only. We could get rid of the negative sign by changing the definition of
\mathchoice{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{k^{{{\mu}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[5.25pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.67499pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}
so that it is past-directed and points from observation point to the source (as originally done by
[
41
]
), but our definition finds a better physical interpretation in terms of the momentum of the gravitons emitted by the source.

Eq.

356
is known as the Braginsky–Thorne formula for the linear memory. Applying it to
Eq.

350
allows us to obtain the physical deviation in the two inertial detectors near infinity. We learn that, in a general scattering problem, there will be a permanent displacement between the inertial detectors stationed at infinity due to the passage of a
\gls
GW.

To see an example of how the memory contribution may look like, let us choose a specific model for the source. A common model for
\gls
GW generation is a binary in a circular orbit, but this would be a single bound state and there would be no change in the second derivative of the quadrupole moment, and hence it will not present (linear, ordinary) memory. Hence, let us choose instead an unbounded problem: two massive bodies in a hyperbolic orbit. An advantage of this model is that we can also compute the metric perturbation during the interaction, and hence see how the metric undergoes a permanent shift. We assume their velocities to be non-relativistic, so the Braginsky–Thorne formula may be approximated by

\mathchoice{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}(t,\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})=\frac{4}{r}\quantity[\sum_{\substack{p \\ \text{out}}} m_p \tensor*{v}{^{(p)}_i} \tensor*{v}{^{(p)}_j} - \sum_{\substack{q \\ \text{in}}} m_q \tensor*{v}{^{(q)}_i} \tensor*{v}{^{(q)}_j}]^{\text{TT}}+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}}.

(357)

Notice that, in fact, each of these terms corresponds to the second derivative of the quadrupole moment of the source, since

\mathchoice{\ddot{Q}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}=2\sum_{p}m_{p}\mathchoice{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{i}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{i}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{i}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{i}}}}\mathchoice{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{j}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{j}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{j}}}}{v^{{{(p)}}}_{{{j}}}}.

(358)

In fact,
Eq.

357
can be obtained directly by working in the quadrupole approximation
[
29
]
. Notice that, in terms of the quadrupole moment, we find

\mathchoice{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}(t,\vec{\boldsymbol{x}})=\frac{2}{r}\mathchoice{\Delta\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{\Delta\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}(t-r)+\order{\frac{1}{r^2}}.

(359)

Consider then two bodies with masses
m_{1}
and
m_{2}
and position vectors
\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{1}
and
\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{2}
. We assume the center of mass to be at rest at the origin. It is convenient to introduce the notation

\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}=\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{1}-\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{2},\quad\mu=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}},\quad\mbox{and}\quad\alpha=Gm_{1}m_{2},

(360)

which is inverted by

\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{1}=\frac{\mu\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}}{m_{1}},\quad\mbox{and}\quad\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}_{2}=-\frac{\mu\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}}{m_{2}}.

(361)

Then, following
[
155
]
, we know that the Newtonian solution for
\vec{\boldsymbol{r}}(t)
is given parametrically as

\displaystyle t

\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{2E}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{2E}}\quantity(e \sinh\xi- \xi),

(362a)

\displaystyle x

\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{2E}\quantity(e - \cosh\xi),

(362b)

\displaystyle y

\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha}{2E}\sqrt{e^{2}-1}\sinh\xi,

(362c)

where
E
is the energy and
e>1
is the orbit’s eccentricity. Using these results, one can find the quadrupole moment. It is given by

\mathchoice{Q^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}=\frac{\alpha^{2}\mu}{4E^{2}}\matrixquantity(\lx@physics@matrix(e - \cosh\xi)^2 & \sqrt{e^2-1}\sinh\xi(e - \cosh\xi) & 0 \\ \sqrt{e^2-1}\sinh\xi(e - \cosh\xi) & (e^2 - 1)\sinh^2\xi& 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\endlx@physics@matrix).

(363)

We still need to project to the
\gls
TT components. Once we do this by using
\mathchoice{\Lambda^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{k}{l}}}_{{{i}{j}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.7052pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.93228pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.55847pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.11319pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Lambda^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{k}{l}}}_{{{i}{j}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.7052pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.93228pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.55847pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.11319pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Lambda^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{k}{l}}}_{{{i}{j}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.7052pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.93228pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.55847pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.11319pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\Lambda^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.82928pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.68811pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.2058pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[3.71356pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.29834pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.64166pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{k}{l}}}_{{{i}{j}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.42017pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.7052pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.93228pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[2.56946pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[1.55847pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[1.11319pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}(\boldsymbol{\hat{z}})
, we get to

\mathchoice{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}=\frac{\alpha^{2}\mu}{8E^{2}}\matrixquantity(\lx@physics@matrix(e - \cosh\xi)^2 - (e^2 - 1)\sinh^2\xi& 2\sqrt{e^2-1}\sinh\xi(e - \cosh\xi) & 0 \\ 2\sqrt{e^2-1}\sinh\xi(e - \cosh\xi) & -(e - \cosh\xi)^2 + (e^2 - 1)\sinh^2\xi& 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\endlx@physics@matrix).

(364)

The next step would be differentiating
\mathchoice{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}
with respect to time. Since we only have
\mathchoice{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{Q^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}
as a function of
\xi
, and
t
as a function of
\xi
, we need to write

\displaystyle\derivative[2]{\tensor*{Q}{^{\text{TT}}_i_j}}{t}

\displaystyle=\derivative{\xi}{t}\derivative{\xi}\quantity(\dv{\tensor*{Q}{^{\text{TT}}_i_j}}{t}),

(365a)

\displaystyle=\derivative{\xi}{t}\derivative{\xi}\quantity(\dv{\xi}{t}\dv{t}\dv{\tensor*{Q}{^{\text{TT}}_i_j}}{\xi}),

(365b)

\displaystyle=\quantity(\dv{t}{\xi})^{-1}\derivative{\xi}\quantity(\qty(\dv{t}{\xi})^{-1}\dv{t}\dv{\tensor*{Q}{^{\text{TT}}_i_j}}{\xi}).

(365c)

The resulting components are

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{x}}}}(t)

\displaystyle=-\mathchoice{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{y}}}}(t)=\frac{2E\quantity[2(e^2 - 1) \sinh^2\xi- \cosh\xi(e \cosh\xi-1)(e + (e^2 -2)\cosh\xi)]}{(e\cosh\xi-1)^{3}},

(366a)

and

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}(t)

\displaystyle=\mathchoice{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{x}}}}{\ddot{Q}^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{y}{x}}}}(t)=\frac{2E\sqrt{e^{2}-1}\sinh\xi\quantity(4 \cosh\xi- e (3 + \cosh(2\xi)))}{(e\cosh\xi-1)^{3}},

(366b)

where
\xi=\xi(t)
.

With these results at hand, we can make a parametric plot of each component of
\mathchoice{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}
against time
t(\xi)
(or, more precisely, retarded time). This is shown in
Fig.

7
, which clearly exhibits that the values of
\mathchoice{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{i}{j}}}}
at early and late times differ by a finite amount.

Figure 7:
Time-dependent gravitational field in the
\gls
TT gauge for a pair of masses with the same mass
m_{1}=m_{2}=$1$
, Newtonian energy
E=$0.01$
and impact parameter
b=$100$
.
R
is the distance from the sources to the observation point (assumed to be perpendicular to the plane of motion of the sources).
u
is the retarded time. Since we are using
G=c=1
units, all values are to be compared to the scales set by the masses
m_{1}=m_{2}
. In the plot, notice how after the masses interact in the neighborhood of
u=0
there is a lasting change in the gravitational field (specifically in the
\mathchoice{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}{h^{{{\text{TT}}}}_{{{x}{y}}}}
component).

Notice that a finite difference between the gravitational field at late and early times is exactly what we found in
Section

6.2
when considering the emission of null radiation to null infinity. Incidentally, the scattering process we considered this time emits null radiation to null infinity in the form of
\glspl
GW. Therefore, the memory effect we are observing in this derivation is a manifestation of a physical realization of a supertranslation. We had foreshadowed this connection by referring to the physical realization of a supertranslation as a “state with memory”. This discussion now justifies the name “memory field” for the
C
field defined in
Eq.

163
.

Above, I described the linear memory effect, originally discussed by
[
255
,
40
,
41
]
. Nevertheless, the memory effect is a much deeper effect.
[
59
]
, and independently
[
32
]
, noticed that the memory effect also has a nonlinear counterpart.
[
229
]
soon interpreted this counterpart as being the linear memory due to the emission of gravitons by the matter sources. Indeed, consider
Eqs.

284
and
159
. We see that the emission of
\glspl
GW to infinity also induces a memory shift. In a black hole binary merger, for example, we get a bound state, and hence the quadrupole will not change significantly at linear order. However, the
\glspl
GW emitted by the binary during the merger can be considered as bodies moving asymptotically inertially. One may then compute the linear memory related to these emitted
\glspl
GW and find the nonlinear contribution. This can be understood as the meaning behind the Bondi news contribution to
\mathchoice{\mathcal{T}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{u}{u}}}}{\mathcal{T}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{u}{u}}}}{\mathcal{T}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{u}{u}}}}{\mathcal{T}^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[4.72806pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[2.80504pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.0036pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{u}{u}}}}
occurring in
Eq.

284
.

A great interest in the memory effect is due to the fact it can be measured in principle, and hence provides an experimental test of the
\gls
IR structure of
\gls
GR. Furthermore, since black hole binaries involve nonlinear memory, it is also a test of the nonlinear nature of Einstein gravity. Current
\gls
GW detectors, such as
\glsxtrshort
LIGO, Virgo, and
\glsxtrshort
KAGRA, cannot detect memory in individual events, the reason being they are not sensitive to the very small frequencies associated to the effect. However, it is possible to combine the measurements of many different events and obtain a coherent result, but a large number of events is necessary. Future experiments, such as
\glsxtrshort
LISA, may be able to detect memory in individual events. For details on measuring memory, see, for example,
[
100
,
117
]
.

For further discussion about the memory effect, see the excellent discussion by
[
29
]
, which also discusses the relation between nonlinear memory and
\gls
CK spacetimes.

6.6
The
\Glsfmtlong
IR Triangle

In
Section

6.4
we saw that supertranslation symmetry and the Weinberg soft graviton theorem are two aspects of the same physical phenomenon. We also reached a similar conclusion concerning supertranslations and the memory effect on
Section

6.5
. This naturally raises a question: are the soft graviton theorem and the memory effect related? If so, how?

They are indeed related, and the connection was given by
[
226
]
. It is merely a Fourier transform and a change of notation and conventions: we need to write the expressions in position space (even though the Weinberg soft theorem is written in momentum space) and account for the different normalizations
